name: Reza Barzegar Nozari
department: Department of Artificial Intelligence, Faculty of Computer Engineering

research.title: Learning from social interactions
research.description: How do trust, influence, and leadership shape collective preferences? My research models relationships between individuals to support personalized and group recommendation.
research.detail: My published work investigates implicit trust-network construction, influence-aware group recommendation, leader impact, and adaptive group formation through multi-agent reinforcement learning. Applications include e-commerce and multi-day tourist itineraries.

research.title: Transferring knowledge efficiently
research.description: How can a smaller model learn the most useful information from a larger one? I explore geometric alignment, optimal transport, and selective teacher supervision.
research.detail: Current manuscripts investigate Wasserstein-based distribution alignment, student-calibrated teacher supervision, and budgeted distillation. These directions examine the relationship between representation geometry and the cost of knowledge transfer.

research.title: Understanding and adapting models
research.description: Which internal components matter for a given input? My recent research explores mechanistic interpretability and causally informed adaptation of large language models.
research.detail: The CRAT manuscript studies causally routed adaptive tuning for machine translation. Related interests include parameter-efficient fine-tuning, probabilistic graphical models, graph neural networks, and uncertainty-aware learning.
